At about 09:30 p.m., when they reached in front of entry gate of Cross River Mall, Parking Main Road, Delhi, all of a sudden, a car Mahindra Xylo bearing registration no. The driver of the offending vehicle came out of the vehicle and Prakhar caught him and on asking he told his name as Kapil @ Gajdender Nagar (respondent no.1 herein) and he was under the influence of alcohol.
Police was called at 100 number.
PCR vehicle came and removed the petitioner to Dr. Hedgewar Hospital, Delhi, where MLC of the petitioner was prepared and he was medically treated.
The petitioner sustained injuries in his right leg and waist.
3. Mentioning the above facts, the petitioner gave statement to police on the basis of which, FIR no.37/2019, under sections 279/337 IPC was registered in the matter at PS Anand Vihar.
After completion of the investigation, DAR was filed before this Tribunal, which has been treated as claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, on behalf of the petitioner/ injured.
Notice of DAR was issued to the respondents but none appeared on behalf of them.

8. I heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and have also perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

9. It is seen that the petitioner/ injured got himself examined as PW1 and testified by way of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A on the lines of the FIR which he had got lodged on the basis of his statement made to police.
PW1/ injured categorically deposed that respondent no.1 was driving the car at a high speed, rashly and negligently and caused his accident which resulted into injuries to him.
PW1 stated that with respect to the accident, FIR no.37/19, PS Anand Vihar was also registered against the respondent no.1 for causing his accident.

The testimony of PW1/ injured has remained unchallenged as this witness was not cross-examined on behalf of the respondents, who neither ______________________________________________________________________ filed reply/ written-statement nor led any evidence in their defence.
Since the testimony of the petitioner has remained controverted, the same has to be accepted on its face value itself.
10. Further, on perusal of the DAR Ex.PW1/4 (colly), this Tribunal finds that the FIR was registered on the same day of the accident.

The FIR shows that when Investigating Officer reached at the spot on receipt of information of the accident vide DD no.67A, dated 31.01.2019, the motorcycle of the injured was found stuck under the offending vehicle.
The Site Plan of the place of the accident which is part of the DAR supports the occurrence of the accident as per version of the injured.

The seizure memo of the offending vehicle and that of the motorcycle of the injured, which are part of the DAR,
shows that the same were seized from the spot of accident itself in accidental condition.
The mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle and that of the vehicle of injured show the accidental damages.

At page no.17 of the DAR, there is MLC no.17/19 of driver/ Kapil @ Gajender Nagar, which shows that on medical examination conducted on 01.02.2019 at 08:00 a.m., the smell of alcohol was found positive with BAC 167 mg/100 ml and this fact further indicates that being under the influence of alcohol, the driver/ respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle in reckless manner resulting into accident of the petitioner.
11.
Furthermore, there is no challenge from the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle to the version of the petitioner.

The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into ______________________________________________________________________ the witness box to challenge the testimony of the injured (PW1) regarding the above accident and its manner but neither he filed a reply to the claim petition nor preferred to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co.

Apart from above, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on a large peripheral field.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the m o t o r v e h i c l e i n a p u b l i c p l a c e , r a t h e r h e ______________________________________________________________________ is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar,
(2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].

sentences.text: (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material losses.

So far non-pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e.
on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."

______________________________________________________________________ 17. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
"4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objective co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."

INTEREST 27.
The petitioner shall also be entitled for the interest @ 7% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization.
LIABILITY 28.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Admittedly, the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident and therefore, the respondent no.1 Kapil @ Gajender Nagar, being the driver of the offending vehicle is the principal tortfeasor, whereas respondent no.2 Ajay Srivastava, its registered owner would have the vicarious liability.
Accordingly, the respondent no. 1 and 2 would have been liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner and their liability shall be joint and several.
RELIEF 29.
In the light of above discussion, the present DAR/ claim petition is allowed and the following award is passed:

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.53,460/- (Rs. Fifty Three Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Only) to the petitioner along with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing of DAR/
petition till realization to be paid by the respondents no.1 & 2, jointly and severally.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner sustained injuries in his right leg and waist.
After completion of the investigation, DAR was filed before this Tribunal, which has been treated as claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, on behalf of the petitioner/ injured.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Vide order dated 15.11.2022, the respondents were proceeded ex-parte and following issues were framed:
1. Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 31.01.2019 at about 09:30 p.m., in front of entry gate of Cross River Mall, Main Road, within the jurisdiction of PS Anand Vihar, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. DL5CE-1474, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co.

3 Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi) 310.
12.
Moreover, the MLC, prepared at Dr. Hedgewar Hospital, Delhi, clearly shows that the petitioner/
injured was brought to the hospital in injured condition with the history of RTA (Road Traffic Accident) and further the injuries suffered by him were opined to be grievous in nature.
13.
Apart from above, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.
14.
Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into grievous injuries to the petitioner.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on a large peripheral field.
[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar,
(2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].
16.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Thus,
keeping in view the nature of injury and the period of treatment, it may be safely assumed that injured would not have been in a position to resume his work which he had been doing prior to the accident, for at least 15 days after the accident and therefore, he is entitled to be compensated for the said period.
This is not the case of petitioners that the injured received any permanent disability as a result of the injuries sustained in the accident and therefore, no compensation can be granted under this head.
Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
23.
The MLC which is part of the DAR, shows that the petitioner sustained chip fracture of right tibia in the accident.
Debridement was done and sutures were applied to treat the said injury and medicines were prescribed and thereafter, he was discharged on the same day with advice to review in OPD after two days.
Thus, considering the nature of injury and period of treatment, it can be safely inferred that the petitioner had to spend a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the purpose Dar-Vineet Kumar vs Kapil @ Gajender Nagar on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29166737/
7 of early recovery apart from incurring transport charges for visiting the hospital on number of occasions for his further treatment and therefore, a notional sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

Thus, it is clear that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner/ injured must have gone through the pain and sufferings during his treatment and therefore, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Thus, the compensation in this case comes to Rs.53,460/-.
The petitioner shall also be entitled for the interest @ 7% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization.
Admittedly, the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident and therefore, the respondent no.1 Kapil @ Gajender Nagar, being the driver of the offending vehicle is the principal tortfeasor, whereas respondent no.2 Ajay Srivastava, its registered owner would have the vicarious liability.
Accordingly, the respondent no. 1 and 2 would have been liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner and their liability shall be joint and several.
RELIEF 29.
In the light of above discussion, the present DAR/ claim petition is allowed and the following award is passed:
This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.53,460/- (Rs. Fifty Three Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Only) to the petitioner along with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing of DAR/
petition till realization to be paid by the respondents no.1 & 2, jointly and severally.

Karkardooma, Delhi, of PO MACT, Shahdara, through RTGS/ NEFT, within 30 days from today.
Disbursement of Award Amount 32.
The Manager, UCO Bank, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi is directed that after compliance of the award amount, the entire award amount shall be released to the petitioner by way of transferring the said amount into his MACT Saving Bank Account.
The petitioner shall open a saving bank account near the place of his residence.
Further, the bank of petitioner is directed to comply with the following conditions: -
(a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e., the savings bank account(s)
of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
(b) The original fixed deposit shall be retained by the bank in safe custody.
